newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL secondaries retrace, blue chips end higher.
newsitem.headline: KL secondaries retrace, blue chips end higher.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur stocks finished the week on a mixed note, with the heated buying in secondary issues giving way to profit-taking but blue chips finishing modestly higher.

Recent sharp losses in Second Board stocks like poultry concern Sin Heng Chan may have given investors pause, one institutional dealer said. "There's some profit-taking as well. A lot of stocks went up quite a lot."
The blue chip-focused Composite Index rose 4.05 points to 1,117.55, while the Second Board index slipped 1.79 points to 572.24 after surging as high as 581.31 earlier in the day.
At the end of the day, volume was very heavy at over 295 million shares with losers beating out gainers by 301 to 263.
Blue chips were weaker in morning trade, but edged up slightly by midsession. Secondary stocks, meanwhile, took the opposite path, giving up all their gains by the afternoon as late selling set in.

Discussing the big run-up in the Second Board, Ralph Dixon of TA Securities' international division said, "We've got to go through these temporary bouts of profit-taking," adding that prices may head yet lower early next week.
